title: Poland Walks a Fiscal Tightrope as Fuel Relief and Rising Debt Collide · 10 Oct
keywords: Poland, fiscal policy, inflation, fuel prices, cost of living, EU deficit, public debt, Andrzej Domański, PiS, European Commission, Eurostat, defence spending, VAT, windfall tax, budget confrontation
notes: Warsaw has launched a fuel-price intervention package designed to cut pump prices and ease household costs, but the move arrives as official data confirm that Polish inflation is rising, not falling. At the same time, the government faces mounting pressure over a deficit that the European Commission projects will reach 7.3 percent of GDP in 2025. Together, the two developments expose the tension at the heart of Polish economic policy: how to provide relief today without sacrificing fiscal credibility tomorrow.
